note.summary: This chunk explains how making a FIG regime claim affects pension contribution tax relief and Foreign Tax Credit Relief (FTCR), then sets out which foreign income and gains qualify for FIG relief. It defines qualifying foreign income, disqualified income, and covers trust income, settlements legislation, transfer of assets abroad (ToAA) provisions, and qualifying foreign gains. Foreign income only qualifies if it arises on or after 6 April 2025, meaning former remittance basis users cannot claim relief for pre-6 April 2025 income/gains even if remitted within their first 4 years back in the UK.

2d748a43d0a370c5.heading: Foreign income and gains (FIG) regime (Self Assessment helpsheet HS266)

caveats: Remittance basis abolished from 6 April 2025; domicile no longer a relevant connecting factor - replaced by tax residence-based system.

If 4-year period as UK resident started before 6 April 2025, FIG regime can be used from 2025-26 tax year up to and including the last tax year of the 4-year period (e.g. those becoming UK resident from 2022-23 can still use it).
Unused years cannot be rolled over if no claim is made for a particular year within the 4-year window.
Once the 4-year qualifying period ends, only way to requalify is a further period of at least 10 consecutive tax years of non-UK residence.
Losing personal allowance, CGT annual exempt amount and other reliefs applies regardless of whether claim is for income only, gains only, or OWR only.
Foreign losses cannot be claimed in the claim year and cannot be carried forward or backward.
This helpsheet must be read together with the relevant notes accompanying supplementary pages; content applies to the 2026 version (2025-26 tax year).

note.summary: HS266 explains the FIG regime, introduced 6 April 2025 to replace the remittance basis, allowing 'qualifying new residents' (UK residents in their first 4 years after 10+ consecutive years of non-UK residence) to claim relief on foreign income and gains via annual claims on SA109 plus relevant supplementary pages (SA103F, SA104F, SA106, SA107, SA108). Claims must be made per tax year and per source, have no monetary limit, but must be made within 12 months of the normal filing date (i.e. by the anniversary of 31 January following the tax year). Making a claim causes loss of personal allowance, CGT annual exempt amount, blind person's allowance, marriage-related tax reductions, and certain loss reliefs (no carry forward/back), while relieved foreign income is disregarded from adjusted net income calculations.
